report:
## Research Findings: Olive Oil and Stroke Risk

Your view is well-supported by current evidence, though with some nuance.

**Randomized controlled trial evidence:** The PREDIMED trial, a landmark randomized primary-prevention study in Spain, found that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil (or nuts) reduced major cardiovascular events by roughly 30% compared to a control lower-fat diet, with benefits **primarily driven by stroke reduction** (https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/pdf/10.1161/hypertensionaha.113.03353; https://neurotrials.ai/trials/stroke/predimed/). This is strong evidence because randomization limits confounding.

**Meta-analyses of observational and intervention studies:** A meta-analysis combining case-control, cohort, and intervention studies (covering ~38,673 participants for stroke) found olive oil consumption inversely associated with combined CHD/stroke risk (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-nutrition/article/olive-oil-consumption-and-risk-of-chd-andor-stroke-a-metaanalysis-of-casecontrol-cohort-and-intervention-studies/79A90337470271D8A8CE2FDC77BD869E). A more recent dose-response meta-analysis of prospective cohorts confirmed olive oil intake is inversely related to cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality, with maximal benefit around 20g/day, though it noted the specific link to stroke alone needs further exploration (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9623257/).

**Large cohort studies:** Spanish cohort data and Harvard's Nurses' Health Study/Health Professionals Follow-up Study also found that replacing saturated fats (butter, margarine) with olive oil lowered CVD and stroke risk (https://www.clinicalnutritionjournal.com/article/S0261-5614(21)00503-3/fulltext).

**Conclusion:** Evidence—including a strong RCT and multiple meta-analyses—supports that higher olive oil consumption, especially replacing saturated fats, is associated with reduced stroke risk, though benefits appear to plateau at moderate intake levels (~20-30g/day) rather than increasing linearly with more consumption.
